question: A \(16\)-quart radiator is filled with water. Four quarts are removed and replaced with pure antifreeze liquid. Then four quarts of the mixture are removed and replaced with pure antifreeze. This is done a third and a fourth time. The fractional part of the final mixture that is water is:
solution:
Track the water, since each refill adds only antifreeze. Using the usual assumption that the liquid is uniformly mixed before each withdrawal, removing \(4\) of the \(16\) quarts removes \(1/4\) of the water then present. Thus each complete withdrawal and refill leaves \(3/4\) of the previous water amount.

The radiator returns to \(16\) quarts after every refill, so its water fraction is also multiplied by \(3/4\) each time. Starting with water fraction \(1\), after four replacements the fraction is
\[
1\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34
=\frac{81}{256}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{81}{256}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
